title: Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management for Wearable IoT Devices with Conformal Prediction
problem: Energy management for battery-powered wearable IoT devices with stochastic ambient energy harvesting; existing point-prediction energy management methods do not account for prediction uncertainty.
motivation: Small form-factor wearable devices have limited battery capacity; frequent recharging reduces quality of service; ambient energy harvesting is stochastic and difficult to predict accurately without uncertainty quantification.
method: Conformal prediction framework for future energy harvest that provides prediction intervals with provable coverage guarantees. Uncertainty regions are leveraged in a Monte Carlo sampling-based energy management algorithm that evaluates multiple decisions across sampled energy scenarios; results are aggregated via lightweight ML model to make near-optimal energy decisions.
key_novelty: Conformal prediction-based approach for energy harvesting with quantified uncertainty, enabling probabilistic energy management decisions with coverage guarantees.
contributions: Conformal prediction framework for energy harvest forecasting with provable coverage (>90% demonstrated)
Monte Carlo sampling-based energy management exploiting uncertainty regions
Lightweight ML aggregation model for near-optimal decisions
Average of 2 J distance from optimal Oracle on real datasets

metrics.accuracy: >90% coverage with tight prediction intervals; average 2 J from optimal Oracle
metrics.other: Quality of service improvement in wearable IoT

primary_theme: Uncertainty-aware energy management for wearable IoT via conformal prediction
